steps.text: We peruse and interpret the past and future of our civilization, as a monk seeks a revelation from his god.
Humans enjoy talking about the possible futures for their civilization, do they not?
At first, we flaunted what little vestige of truth we managed to grasp, and attempted to converse with the 'gods'.
We were answered with silence.
Then, we began to observe the fates of our own kind—
Some were less advanced than us, some slightly more so... in the end, what we learned was that death was the inevitable end of all the creations of nature.
And so humanity inferred that this was the revelation the gods never spoke.

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: In an instant, we thought we had grasped the truth of the universe.

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: We carefully 'monopolized' the revelation gained through sacrifice, and preached the inevitability of doom with so-called optimism.

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: 'Death is the inevitable end of all the creations of nature. All we can do is to leave behind the truth before our doom.'

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: You've lived on that ship for some time, and come to know some adorable lifeforms. Do you agree with this assessment?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: You don't agree with the Presence?

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: I respect them.

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: They were great people, but most of them were simply fools slightly smarter than the others.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Why are you asking me this? And... why have you brought me here?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: We were in that corridor just a moment ago.

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: Here or there, it makes no difference.

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: You have too many questions, questions that this place can answer.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: What is this place?

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: The graveyard of civilization's memory.
Towering statues made of unknown materials stand upon the vast expanse.
Ripples spread outwards in every direction, up towards the sky beyond the dark clouds, and down towards the grey-white ground.

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: Out in the vastness of the universe, civilization was born, like a drop of water falling into the ocean, leaving ripples in its wake.

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: They cross paths, love, hate, and eventually die.

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: The ripples of dead civilizations are forever etched upon this tombstone. Even after the bright stars of the forebears who inspired so many that came after them are long gone—

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: They still leave behind an incomparable impact on the universe. It is the ripples they left behind that form this land upon which we stand.

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: Their legacy fosters new civilizations, which in turn leave their own traces upon the universe.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: But it seems... broken? Like a tree trunk snapped in half.

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: You're not the first to describe it that way.

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: Once, someone very important to me said the same.

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: An absolute, ultimate presence tirelessly reaps the branches that sprout from this poor trunk, yet we know nothing about It.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: What you've shown me is like... a miracle...

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: You saved me... from disintegration...

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: ...God.

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: 'God'?

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: I'm just a humble linguist attempting to explain the universe.

steps.name: Gentle Voice
steps.text: My name is Priestess.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: And, strictly speaking, I did not save you.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Your death has already occurred. I did not intervene in the process of matter being converted to information.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: But material destruction is not true death. Information is not so easily erased, and your information was stored in Originium.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: B-But I can think. I felt I was living when I was on the ship. All this vivid—

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: A stream of data repeated over and over.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: I intentionally left behind fragments of history in order to observe our past lives.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: So this is like a dream?

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: 'Dream' is vague and subjective. Do not allow language to lead you to meaningless self-doubt, before you have touched its fundamental nature.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: You may understand this as a snapshot from the past that I have recorded in the form of information.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: But it's nothing more than a still frame. There is no future for it.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Then why am I here?

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: I saw you at the instant of your death.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Someone disturbed me. It was a coincidence, a whim of probability.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: So... I'm not special.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Oh but you are, Hierda. You, and those like you, are very special.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Originium has shaped you into what you are. You have interacted with Originium in wondrous ways.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Your history and your civilization all exist because of Originium.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: But Originium has also brought so much pain...

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Yes. It was a mistake. Your existence was not part of the plan.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Do you mean that the people on Terra shouldn't exist?

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: No, you misunderstand.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Your civilization was born of probability. Just like you, standing here right now, it exists in time on an objective basis.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Born of probability, and lost to probability. It is the most basic rule of the universe.
The Cautus needs time to digest it all.
Originium brought destruction to her, but also consolation and infinite knowledge in this frozen time.
She feels lonely, but no pain. If there is one thing right now that could cause pain, it would be—

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Terra... my home...

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: It was not blessed by God...
She turns around to look behind her.
The land stretches as far as the eye can see, rippling like mountains extending infinitely.
She cannot see the end, nor any trace of Terra.
But she knows that the land is just within reach, if she only stretched out her hand.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Terra.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Is it doomed...?
The 'god' looks up at the megastructure and does not answer.

a.text: Does that future you're always talking about really exist?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor, be careful!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Originium activity in this area far exceeds Dr. Kal'tsit's estimations. Originium crystals are growing at a breakneck pace...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Plus those strange enemies that keep appearing—
Yet your attention is drawn to the Originium in front of you.
Every shard, every facet...
Reflects the same scene in your eyes—

options: Her silhouette appears on every facet.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: I am curious about you, Hierda.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: From here, I can observe everything of your world. You are the second being from this civilization to interact with me.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Do you still love your so-called 'great land'?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I think so... yes...

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Even if the pain that it brings you is real and inexorable?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Yes...

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Is this what concerns you?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I... I'm not sure what you mean.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Only praise for life and the indomitable will. Death has not overcome you.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: You came to me in search of an answer regarding the future. We stand now before that answer—

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: One that cannot be described by language.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: —What is it?!

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Remember that absolute, ultimate presence I mentioned?

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: It was once thought to be light from a distant star.
The Cautus looks up almost instinctively. Dark clouds cover the sky, blanketing the plain in darkness.
Then, a faint light breaks through a crack in the clouds. Looking upon the light, masses of people cheer and exclaim.
The Cautus feels as though she were among those masses.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I'm witnessing—

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: History.
Then, the ray of light bursts into a rainbow spectrum, as though the universe were painting upon a black canvas.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: In their last moments, the pious souls continued to pray to the mysterious blessing of the universe.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: The people of reason, the scientists, they boarded their flying machines and flew into the light, hoping to touch the truth up close.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: (There's no movement? Why isn't anything happening, now that they've gone into the light?)

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: The idealists, the conservatives, denounced the enemy for invading the space that had belonged to them from their first moment of sentience.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: They brashly directed their most dangerous weapons towards the prismatic sky.
The gentle light accepted all, neither exploding nor fighting back.
The light followed its determined path, ignoring the agitated souls beneath, though chaos and death had already begun to spread amongst them.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: W-What's happening?

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Do you want to go into the light?
The Cautus feels her vision climb upwards, over the agitated crowd, over the burning mountains, over the dark clouds.
She can almost reach out and touch the rainbow light.
Weapons powerful enough to destroy an entire planet fly past her into the light without a sound. Ships that can sail the stars fall powerlessly to the ground.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: They resisted.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: They prayed.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: They tried to sway the cold light with all things bright and beautiful that they had created over millennia—

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: But the light was unwavering, cold like deep space.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: The light passed over the planet and left. All was silent.
The Cautus finds herself gazing into deep space, at the broken remains of the celestial body.
It is like the sight that the Presence was gazing at, that she was curious about, when she gazed upon the Presence.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: It's... all gone... why?
From whence did the doom come? Why did it come? Did it leave? Where did it go? What happened to all the lives—
Then she sees it.

Only broken remains are left upon the ruined surface of the planet, when the light of the star once again shines upon it. The planetary fragments break through the bonds of gravity and scatter to infinite space.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: It was once a flourishing civilization that marked those fragments.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: No one could ever be prepared for It.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Even the wisest, most knowledgeable sages of this civilization had hoped for some premonition, some warning before the coming of the doom.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Unfortunately...
The Cautus witnessed the death of the gods, the powerlessness of the gods. For a moment, she even forgot how to fear.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Is this... the history that you experienced?

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: No. It's simply one of countless fragments that we captured.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: This single glimpse could hardly compare to what I experienced for myself.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: The answer that you seek is not yet complete. Listen to the sounds that emerge from the ruins.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: The rocks that come from deep space—

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Comets. Sometimes, they are the bringers of the seed of life; other times, they do little more than fill the silence of a dead planet.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Where do they come from?

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Anywhere, perhaps even another destroyed planet, the marks of a lost civilization still etched upon it.
The gravity of the dead planet begins to draw in guests from deep space, and it begins to be made whole again.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Those ships floating in deep space—

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Explorers, seekers, colonizers, perhaps even plunderers, coming from far away.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: They, too, accelerate the evolution of civilization.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Do you mean that's what happened to Terra?

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Your greed has gotten the better of your fear.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: What you learn cannot be unlearned, Hierda. Having glimpsed a vestige of truth, are you willing to go back into the darkness of ignorance?
The Cautus continues to stand before the imposing 'gravestone'.
She touches the ripples upon it and trembles.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Every mark is the end of a civilization... only now do I truly feel—

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Can I stay here and learn?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: You have shown me the key to the answer. I have to comprehend all this knowledge on my own.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Even though this is only a fragment of time, frozen forever?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: ...Yes.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: You're very much like us.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: You may roam this place and anywhere on Rhodes Island freely, to seek the answer that you crave.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: As for whether you want to stay here, or go back to the Terra that you loved so much...

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: I will respect whatever choice you make. We will meet again soon.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Y-You're leaving? Where are you going?

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Someone has been waiting for me.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: ...For far too long.

a.text: Unauthorized 3rd-party plugin deleted. Default settings restored.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I've received your inquiry, Closure.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: PRTS is denying all access requests. We've lost administrator permissions and we do not have the ability to retake PRTS.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Kal'tsit?!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Finally, an answer!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Where are you? The Doctor and Amiya are coming over to help!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Bad news. PRTS is taking over all equipment on the ship, including the engines.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I know. I'm fighting for Rhodes Island's last chance.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Closure, warn the Doctor and Amiya—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: She's waking up.
